decisions.reason: The candidate already records the source message's distinct four-layer decision; resizing the main-board outline to 70×50 does not change the layer count.
The 70×50 resize applies to the legacy main board, not the power board's dimensions, orientation, mounting, or aspect ratio.

The source reiterates enclosure rails and modular cabling but does not change the established connector alignment, edge placement, or access rules; the rejection of connector consolidation belongs to the interboard interface Requirement.
The client explicitly rejects consolidating the individual JST connections into a large connector and requires retaining the modular per-sensor cabling arrangement.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Based on my rough math: on a 70×50 board (3500mm²), components take about 1300mm² (~37% coverage) — that's well within normal PCB density and should route cleanly on 4 layers.

I'd prefer to keep the individual JST connectors rather than consolidate to a 2x15+10p. The modular approach is important for the enclosure, each sensor has its own clean cable, and the boards slide into rails. A single big connector with a fan-out ribbon cable would make the wiring inside the enclosure very messy and hard to service.
Since you already have all the components placed in KiCad, could you just resize the board outline to 70×50 and do a rough rearrangement? I'm not skilled in KiCad, it would take me hours to do what would take you minutes since you already have the full project open. I'd really appreciate if you could try the resize on your end.

Noted about the ESP32 on the edge, that's fine.

value_updates.connector_consolidation_policy: Retain the individual JST connectors and separate sensor cables; do not consolidate them into a 2x15+10p connector with a fan-out ribbon cable.

decisions.reason: Resizing the legacy main board and retaining individual connectors do not change the four-board topology or the identity of the separate boards.
The candidate already records the same message's acceptance of placing the ESP32 at the board edge; the 70×50 resize supplies no additional antenna-placement or clearance change.
The four-layer statement concerns the resized legacy main board, while this candidate governs the power-board layer stack.
The source concerns the legacy main-board connector architecture and outline; it does not alter power-board battery-connector placement, orientation, spacing, or mounting-hole clearance.
The main-board resize and per-sensor JST cabling decision do not change the LED daughterboard's form, LED count, or selected LED component.
The source does not change the charge-status display method, external charge-LED interface, connector, signal, or resistor configuration.
The main-board mechanical resize and connector-layout decision do not alter DCDC1 voltage programming, current rating, or rail-regulation behavior.
Retaining individual sensor cables does not itself change the established cable-length range, I2C speed, pull-ups, or optional series-resistor policy.
